chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Jameel, from one of our companions, from one of the two (Imams) (peace be upon him), who said:
When the guardian of the killed person dies, his son stands in his place after him regarding the blood money (diyah).
ai.seo_question: Who inherits the right to claim blood money if the original guardian of the deceased dies?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the mechanism of inheritance regarding the right to claim blood money (diyah), establishing that the son succeeds the father as the primary guardian (wali) in cases of homicide. In Shia jurisprudence, this underscores the continuity of the victim's family authority to seek retribution or compensation, ensuring the legal standing remains within the direct lineage. It reflects the broader Islamic legal principle that rights attached to the person or family unit are transferable to heirs unless specified otherwise.
